cancellationtokenregistration-disposal-b.title: Match CancellationTokenRegistration lifetime to the registered callback owner
cancellationtokenregistration-disposal-b.short: Dispose obsolete registrations to release callback state
cancellationtokenregistration-disposal-b.summary: CancellationToken.Register returns a CancellationTokenRegistration that can be disposed to unregister the callback. Lifetime management matters especially when short-lived objects register with long-lived tokens.
cancellationtokenregistration-disposal-b.why: Leaving registrations attached can keep callback state reachable from the token source and extend object lifetimes unnecessarily.
cancellationtokenregistration-disposal-b.tips: Give each registration a clear owner and normally dispose it with using or the owning component. Also account for cancellation racing with disposal.

process-redirected-output-drain-before-e.title: Drain redirected Process output while waiting for the child to exit
process-redirected-output-drain-before-e.short: Do not let full stdout or stderr pipes block the child process
process-redirected-output-drain-before-e.summary: Redirected Process standard output and error travel through bounded pipes. A child that writes heavily requires the parent to consume those streams concurrently.
process-redirected-output-drain-before-e.why: Waiting for exit before reading redirected streams can leave the child blocked writing to a full pipe while the parent waits for that child to exit.
process-redirected-output-drain-before-e.tips: Start reading both stdout and stderr before awaiting process exit, run those reads concurrently, and await the read tasks before consuming their final results.

taskcompletionsource-run-continuations-a.title: Separate TaskCompletionSource continuations from the thread that signals completion
taskcompletionsource-run-continuations-a.short: RunContinuationsAsynchronously reduces surprising inline continuation execution
taskcompletionsource-run-continuations-a.summary: Completing a TaskCompletionSource can make awaiting continuations runnable. RunContinuationsAsynchronously keeps those continuations from executing inline on the completion-signaling call path.
taskcompletionsource-run-continuations-a.why: Inline continuation execution can re-enter consumer code from SetResult while locks are held or internal state is being updated, creating latency and deadlock hazards.
taskcompletionsource-run-continuations-a.tips: Consider the option for library boundaries and completion sources whose Task is exposed to independent consumers unless synchronous continuation behavior is intentionally required.

executioncontext-flow-suppression-bounda.title: Keep ExecutionContext flow suppression tightly scoped
executioncontext-flow-suppression-bounda.short: Suppress ambient-state flow only for work that deliberately does not need it
executioncontext-flow-suppression-bounda.summary: ExecutionContext carries ambient state such as AsyncLocal values across asynchronous and threading boundaries. SuppressFlow explicitly prevents that automatic propagation.
executioncontext-flow-suppression-bounda.why: Suppressing flow too broadly can drop correlation, culture, or other ambient state that application behavior depends on, turning a performance tweak into a semantic bug.
executioncontext-flow-suppression-bounda.tips: Reserve suppression for low-level work dispatch that intentionally needs no ambient state, keep the scope short, and prefer normal context flow in ordinary application code.
